_note: Sources for Form 2 Maths (Batch M2-1, Term 1). Computed answers follow the rules named here; 'checked' says how far each rule was verified.

integers.ref: Standard rules for operations on integers (the set ℤ), as in Form 2 mathematics textbooks
integers.supports: Order on the number line; adding with the same or different signs; subtracting as adding the opposite; signs of products and quotients; multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.
integers.checked: Standard result; the computed answers are checked by code. Not externally sourced: compare with the pupil's textbook.

powers.ref: Definition of a whole number power (base, index or exponent)
powers.supports: aⁿ is a multiplied by itself n times; a negative base with an even index gives a positive number, with an odd index a negative number; 10ⁿ has n zeros.
powers.checked: Standard definition; the values are computed by code.

laws-of-indices.ref: Laws of indices for powers of the same base
laws-of-indices.supports: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; a⁰ = 1 for a ≠ 0; the laws need the same base.
laws-of-indices.checked: Standard result; the indices are computed by code.

primes.ref: Definition of prime and composite numbers; the fundamental theorem of arithmetic (unique prime factorisation)
primes.supports: A prime has exactly two factors; 1 is not prime; 2 is the only even prime; every whole number above 1 has one prime factorisation.
primes.checked: Standard result; primality and factorisations are computed by code (src/engine/lib/maths2.js, tested).

hcf-lcm.ref: Definitions of the highest common factor (HCF, also highest common divisor) and lowest common multiple (LCM); the prime-factor method; HCF × LCM = a × b for two numbers
hcf-lcm.supports: HCF: largest number dividing both; LCM: smallest number in both times tables; with prime factors, the lowest powers of the common primes (HCF) and the highest powers of all primes (LCM). Which situations need the HCF or the LCM is an authored judgement.
hcf-lcm.checked: Standard result; values computed by code (hcf, lcm in src/engine/lib/maths2.js, tested). The HCF/LCM sorting card is authored: please check the wording.

roots.ref: Definitions of square roots and cube roots of whole numbers
roots.supports: √n² = n and ∛n³ = n for whole numbers n; with prime factors, halve the indices (square root) or divide them by three (cube root); a number between two squares has a square root between their roots.
roots.checked: Standard result; values computed by code.

sequences.ref: Arithmetic sequences (common difference) and sequences that multiply by a common ratio
sequences.supports: Next term = last term + d; term n = first term + (n − 1) × d; next term of a multiplying sequence = last term × r.
sequences.checked: Standard result; values computed by code.

triangle-inequality.supports: In a triangle each side is less than the sum of the other two; equality means the three points are on one line; the third side lies strictly between the difference and the sum of the other two.
triangle-inequality.checked: Standard result; the tests are computed by code (triangleOk). The statements about the equal case are authored.

segment.ref: Notation used in Cameroonian mathematics (French-influenced), as in Form 1: (AB) line, [AB) half line, [AB] segment, AB length; midpoint; a point M is on [AB] exactly when AM + MB = AB
segment.supports: Which brackets name which figure; the midpoint halves the length; the parts of a segment add up to the whole.
segment.checked: Notation as approved for Form 1 (line-notation, TR-M); compare with the pupil's exercise book. Lengths computed by code.

perpendicular-bisector.ref: Definition and ruler-and-compasses construction of the perpendicular bisector (mediator) of a segment; its characteristic property: the points equidistant from the end points
perpendicular-bisector.supports: Through the midpoint and perpendicular; compass opening more than half the segment, same opening from both ends; PA = PB exactly when P is on the perpendicular bisector.
perpendicular-bisector.checked: Standard result. The construction steps and the statement pools are authored: please check them against the textbook.

coordinates.ref: Cartesian coordinates in the plane: x-axis and y-axis, origin O(0, 0), ordered pair (abscissa, ordinate)
coordinates.supports: The first coordinate (abscissa) is read along the x-axis, the second (ordinate) along the y-axis; points on the x-axis have ordinate 0 and on the y-axis abscissa 0; moving right/left changes the abscissa, up/down the ordinate.
coordinates.checked: Standard definitions; the drawings and answers are computed by code (coordPlane). The vocabulary pool is authored.

algebra-language.ref: Conventions for writing algebraic expressions (number before letter, no × sign, 1x written x) and the vocabulary variable, term, coefficient, constant term
algebra-language.supports: Translating words into expressions; terms carry the sign in front of them; the coefficient of x is 1 and of −x is −1.
algebra-language.checked: Standard conventions; expressions are built by code (poly, mono). Please check the wording of the phrases against the textbook.

like-terms.ref: Definition of like terms (same letters with the same powers)
like-terms.supports: Like terms differ only in their coefficient; ab = ba; x and x² are unlike; like terms are added by adding their coefficients.
like-terms.checked: Standard result; sums computed by code.

simplify.ref: Simplifying expressions by collecting like terms, and multiplying monomials
simplify.supports: Collect each kind of like term with its sign; multiply numbers then letters; a × a = a².
simplify.checked: Standard result; results computed by code.

substitution.ref: Substituting numbers for letters in an expression, with the order of operations (powers, then × and ÷, then + and −)
substitution.supports: Negative values go in brackets; letters side by side are multiplied; kx² = k × x².
substitution.checked: Standard rule; values computed by code.

expansion.ref: The distributive law a(b + c) = ab + ac
expansion.supports: Every term inside is multiplied by the term outside; a negative factor changes every sign; x × x = x².
expansion.checked: Standard result; expansions computed by code (bracket, poly).

equations.ref: Solving linear equations in one unknown by doing the same operation to both sides
equations.supports: Undo + and − first, then × and ÷; check by substituting.
equations.checked: Standard method; every equation is built from its solution by code, so the answer is exact.

inequalities.supports: Adding, subtracting, and multiplying or dividing by a positive number keep the sign; multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses it.
inequalities.checked: Standard result; solutions and drawings computed by code (holds, ineqLine). The phrases “at least”, “at most”, “more than”, “fewer than” are authored.
